story.title: Three Killed in Los Angeles News Helicopter Crash
story.summary: A news helicopter crashed in Los Angeles while covering a bus collision, resulting in the deaths of three individuals, including a journalist and the pilot. The crash occurred near the scene of a previous accident that had already claimed two lives. Tributes have begun to emerge for the victims.

explore_lenses.label: How was the helicopter crash linked to the bus wreck?
explore_lenses.title: Nearby events, but separate investigations
explore_lenses.summary: The helicopter was covering the earlier Metro bus collision in Chatsworth, but authorities have not said the two crashes had a common cause. The day’s death toll reflects two distinct incidents occurring roughly two hours apart.

claims.text: LAFD logged the bus-and-SUV collision at 5:03 p.m. near Nordhoff Street and De Soto Avenue; it logged the helicopter crash at 6:57 p.m. at 9151 North Mason Avenue.
The bus collision killed two people and sent six others to hospitals, according to LAFD; the later helicopter crash killed three people.

LAPD told NBC Los Angeles that the SUV driver would be arrested after release from the hospital on suspicion of murder; police said they suspected reckless driving, a red-light violation and possible DUI.

explore_lenses.uncertainty_note: No authority has identified a causal connection between the vehicle collision and the helicopter’s loss of control; the bus crash and aircraft crash are being handled on separate tracks.

explore_lenses.label: What is known about why the helicopter went down?
explore_lenses.title: The cause remains unestablished
explore_lenses.summary: There is video and eyewitness material describing the helicopter’s final moments, but neither establishes a mechanical, operational or medical cause. The NTSB is leading the fact-finding process with FAA involvement.

claims.text: The NTSB said it was investigating the September 15 crash of a Eurocopter AS 350 B2 in Chatsworth and expected investigators to arrive at the scene on September 16.
AP reported that an alarm was audible in the cockpit on the crew’s final live video as the helicopter lost altitude, but reported no immediate explanation for the crash.
A witness told NBC Los Angeles the aircraft appeared to be swaying shortly before it fell, while another described a fireball after impact.

explore_lenses.label: What should readers watch for next?
explore_lenses.title: A federal aviation inquiry and a criminal case
explore_lenses.summary: The immediate next developments are expected to be an NTSB preliminary account of the helicopter crash and further action in the separate bus-crash case. A final aviation finding will take substantially longer and is not a near-term answer.

claims.text: LAFD said the NTSB and FAA would handle the helicopter-crash investigation after firefighters assessed four patients, pronounced three dead and transported one person to a hospital.
Forecast: NTSB guidance says a general-aviation preliminary report is typically available within about two weeks, while a final report with analysis and probable cause often takes 12 to 24 months.
The NTSB says its process can include on-scene evidence gathering, analysis, a final probable-cause determination and safety recommendations; it does not determine cause while on scene.

In the separate road-crash case, LAPD told NBC Los Angeles the injured SUV driver would be arrested on suspicion of murder after hospital release, but the reporting did not identify filed charges or a court date.

story_report.summary: Three people were killed when a helicopter crashed in Chatsworth, Los Angeles, while covering a bus collision. The dead included journalist Eliana Moreno and pilot George Marciniw; the third victim has not been publicly identified. The aircraft went down less than two hours after the road crash, which killed two people and injured six others, according to the Los Angeles Fire Department. Federal investigators are examining the helicopter crash, while police are separately pursuing the vehicle-collision case.

sections.heading: Chatsworth crashes followed separate timelines
sections.body: LAFD logged the collision between a bus and SUV near Nordhoff Street and De Soto Avenue at 5:03 p.m. It recorded the helicopter crash at 6:57 p.m. at 9151 North Mason Avenue. LAFD said two people died in the road crash and six were taken to hospitals. LAPD told NBC Los Angeles that the SUV driver would be arrested after leaving the hospital on suspicion of murder; police suspected reckless driving, a red-light violation and possible DUI.

sections.heading: Federal investigators examine helicopter loss
sections.body: The NTSB said it was investigating the September 15 crash of a Eurocopter AS 350 B2 in Chatsworth, with investigators expected at the scene the following day. LAFD said the NTSB and FAA would handle the investigation after firefighters assessed four patients, pronounced three dead and took one person to a hospital. AP reported an audible cockpit alarm in the final live video as the helicopter lost altitude, but no immediate explanation for the crash was reported. NTSB guidance says a preliminary report is generally available in about two weeks, while a final probable-cause report can take 12 to 24 months.

unresolved.text: Authorities have not identified a causal connection between the road collision and the helicopter’s loss of control; the two crashes are being handled separately.
Released information does not establish whether the cockpit alarm, flight behavior, weather, maintenance, pilot actions or another factor contributed to the helicopter crash.
The third person killed in the helicopter crash has not been publicly identified, and the conditions of people hospitalized in connection with the crashes remain incomplete.

related_stories.title: Rodrigo Duterte Appears in Court at The Hague for ICC Proceedings
related_stories.summary: Former Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte made his first appearance before judges at the International Criminal Court (ICC) in The Hague. The 81-year-old is facing accusations of crimes against humanity, with discussions regarding his health and memory impairment taking place during the session.

related_stories.title: Saudi Arabia Claims Houthi Drone Targeted Mecca, Warns of Consequences
related_stories.summary: Saudi Arabia has accused Yemen's Houthi rebels of attempting to attack Mecca, Islam's holiest city, claiming its air defenses intercepted and destroyed a drone deployed by the Houthis. The Saudi-led coalition emphasized that the security of Mecca is a 'red line' and warned of potential deterrent measures. In response, the Houthis have denied the allegations, labeling them as false.

related_stories.title: Escalating Conflict: Houthis Claim Downing Saudi Jet, Saudis Accuse of Drone Attack Near Mecca
related_stories.summary: The Houthi militia in Yemen has claimed to have downed a Saudi jet, while the Saudi-led coalition accused the Houthis of launching a drone attack near Mecca, which the Houthis denied. This exchange of accusations marks a significant escalation in the ongoing conflict, with the Houthis also threatening Saudi oil exports by seizing parts of Yemen's Red Sea.

related_stories.title: House Panel Holds Leon Black in Contempt Over Epstein Investigation
related_stories.summary: The House Oversight Committee voted to hold billionaire Leon Black in contempt for failing to comply with subpoenas related to its investigation into Jeffrey Epstein. Survivors of Epstein have expressed support for the committee's decision and are urging for prosecution against Black following his contempt conviction.
